subject: Clarify: what Redwood retains by default (requests vs outputs)
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme-corp.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question: default retention — are prompts treated as logs?

Camila,

Quick one from our security team while we're on the SOC timeline: can you confirm what Redwood retains by default for hosted API requests? Specifically:
- Do you store raw prompts (user-provided input) and full model outputs?
- Is response metadata (latency, model id, token counts) persisted by default?
- Are streaming/partial outputs (when using SSE) captured as saved artifacts?

We attached our questionnaire (acme-soc2-questionnaire.xlsx) with a few related fields. If you have a short factsheet or single-page summary it would be super helpful.

Thanks,

Jordan — thanks for sending this over and for the attachments. Looping in Ben (sales) and Karthik (product/infra) to make sure we give you the right compliance-level language.

Short answer up front: by default we retain request metadata and model outputs for a limited retention window to support debugging, billing, and quality monitoring. Prompts (the raw user input) are only retained in the same collection when customers do not opt into prompt-stripping; many enterprise contracts can change this default.

I'll let Karthik add the precise definitions and TTLs — see below for a quick bullets summary we can use in your questionnaire.

Camila Reyes

Subject: RE: Question: default retention — are prompts treated as logs?

Hi Jordan — detail from product/infra side below. I tried to keep this practical for your questionnaire fields.

What Redwood stores by default (hosted API):
- Request metadata: request ID, timestamp, model version, region, token count, latency metrics. Persisted for the default metrics retention window (90 days) to power billing & observability.
- Model outputs: full textual outputs generated by the model are stored by default for 45 days. We use outputs for quality monitoring, eval triggers, and to support customer support investigations.
- Raw prompts (user-provided input): by default these are stored for 45 days if they are required to reproduce an issue or deliver a feature (e.g., eval prompt sets). For customers who opt for prompt-stripping in console or via contract, inputs are not stored beyond ephemeral processing and are excluded from persistent logs.
- Streaming fragments / partial outputs: streaming fragments are treated as part of the final output artifact; we persist the assembled final output only. Temporary SSE fragments are buffered in memory and not written to long-term stores unless the request completes and the output is saved.
- KV cache / in-memory acceleration artifacts: never written to durable logs; strictly ephemeral to the serving runtime.

Optional controls (what you can request):
- Prompt stripping: disables persistent storage of raw inputs (recommended for PII-sensitive flows).
- Shorter retention: enterprise settings can reduce the TTL for outputs/metadata (contract term).
- Audit-only mode: store metadata but redact textual output content.

I'll attach a short factsheet with exact TTLs and links to our deletion runbook. Happy to add contract language for your procurement team.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — that helps a lot. Couple follow-ups from the SOC reviewer:
- Can you confirm whether outputs are encrypted at rest and whether encryption keys are customer-managed for Private deployments?
- For streaming use cases where we intentionally drop partial outputs, can we configure the API/SDK to never persist assembled outputs (i.e., ephemeral-only)?

If you have short contract wording we can drop into our procurement process that says "Redwood will not persist raw customer inputs beyond X days unless explicitly enabled", that would move things forward.

Best,
Jordan

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme-corp.com>, camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Question: default retention — are prompts treated as logs?

Jordan — quick reply to finish the thread and propose next steps.

- Encryption: yes — outputs and stored artifacts are encrypted at rest. For Redwood Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and can document the configuration we typically include in enterprise SOWs.
- Ephemeral-only streaming: we offer an "ephemeral mode" flag for API requests that marks the request as non-persistent; when set the runtime processes but does not write assembled outputs to durable logs. This is available for Dedicated/Private customers by config and for hosted customers via an enterprise opt-in.
- Contract language: see suggested clause below you can include in your MSA: "Redwood will not persist raw customer inputs beyond 30 days unless the customer elects prompt retention in writing; upon request Redwood will remove persisted inputs within 72 hours subject to standard audit procedures." We're happy to tighten TTLs in the SOW.

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll return a one-page clause for your procurement team (I can draft and send today).
2) Karthik will attach deletion runbook references for SOC reviewers.

If helpful I can book a 30-minute call with product/security next week to walk through the questionnaire.

Thanks,
